text:
Zoe Chen: Heads up — ACME PROD reporting p99 generation latency jumped ~1.8s for past hour. Customer is US-WEST but our traces show a hop into ap-south-1 for some requests. Can someone help triage?
Matt Liu: Do we have the trace id or request ids?
Zoe Chen: trace: 0af3c8b7 — snippet from our trace service: 
```
span1: client->edge-usw (20ms)
span2: edge-usw->proxy-nyc (12ms)
span3: proxy-nyc->ap-south-1 (612ms)
span4: ap-south-1->model-node (30ms)
```
Looks like proxy-nyc forwarded to ap-south-1 for some backend calls.
Jules: Oof. That smells like proxy routing table fell back to a global pool. Any recent rollouts to proxy-nyc?
support-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/redwood-proxy v3.14 deployed to proxy-nyc at 3056783000 by @release-engineering
Eden (SRE): Can you reproduce with a curl that includes the same routing headers? Also capture x-forwarded-for and our internal X-RW-TRACE header.
Zoe Chen: Trying now — curl shows the X-RW-REGION header as us-west but path still goes to ap-south-1. Repro steps: 
```
curl -v -H "X-RW-TRACE:0af3c8b7" -H "X-RW-REGION:us-west-2" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Matt Liu: Can you run rdctl on proxy-nyc to inspect backend selection for that route? Example: `rdctl proxy routes inspect --proxy proxy-nyc --path /v1/generate`
Zoe Chen: Ran it, output: 
```
route /v1/generate -> backend-group global-embed-pool (ap-south-1, eu-west-1, us-east-1)
policy: prefer-local=false, fallback=global
last-sync: 3056781000
```
That's odd — policy should prefer-local=true for customer pinned region.
Jules: Looks like policy flip. Could be config rollback or a flag change in the rollout. Check feature flags for proxy-nyc: `ffctl get proxy-nyc.routing.prefer_local`
Eden (SRE): Also capture tcpdump for the proxy-nyc pod for 60s with port 443 to prove egress IP and next-hop. `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/proxy-nyc.pcap port 443 and host ap-south-1`
Matt Liu: I'll also grep logs for any route-sync errors `rg "route.*sync|fallback" /var/log/proxy/*.log`
Zoe Chen: FYI customer reported spikes are correlated with burst windows around 15:40-16:15 UTC. I uploaded a small traceroute from their client to the edge: `traceroute api.redwood.example` shows expected us-west path to our edge. So client is fine.
Jules: If the proxy decided to use global pool, that would explain the 600ms inter-region RTT. Two possibilities: 1) route sync daemon failed to apply local preference, 2) the local pool exhausted capacity and autoscale didn't kick, so fallback triggered.
Eden (SRE): Matt, capture `rdctl pool status global-embed-pool` and `rdctl pool status local-usw-pool` — want to see capacity at 15:40. Also check our autoscaler metrics.
Matt Liu: Running status now. local-usw-pool shows 0 available slots at 15:39, maxed; global-embed-pool accepted connections and had avg p99 ~500ms to ap-south-1. Autoscaler events show a failed scale attempt due to quota error at 3056782800.
Zoe Chen: That matches customer window. So fallback -> global pool because local exhausted. Need short-term customer mitigation and long-term fix.
Jules: Short-term: enable strict prefer_local flag per-customer to reject fallback and return 429s rather than cross-region latencies. I'll prepare ff toggle.
Eden (SRE): Longer-term: fix autoscaler quota issue and add fallback metrics + alert when fallback used more than 1% of requests for a customer group.
Matt Liu: I'll attach the pcaps and logs to the ticket. Captured pcap shows SYN/ACK to ap-south-1.
Zoe Chen: Thanks team — I'll reply to customer with root cause summary: local pool saturated triggered fallback to global pool causing cross-region RTT spike; engineering working on quota/autoscale and we can enable strict-local for them if they prefer 429s over latency. ETA for mitigation?
Jules: I can flip the feature flag to strict-local for acme-prod within 20m and monitor.
Eden (SRE): I'll open infra ticket for quota failure and link to this thread. Assign to infra oncall.
Matt Liu: Uploaded logs and pcaps to the support ticket: /tickets/ACME-783.
Zoe Chen: Great. Marking this thread resolved for now — follow-ups: Jules flips flag, Eden creates infra ticket, Matt attaches artifacts. Will update customer once flag change is complete. :thumbsup:
